newsitem.title: GERMANY: German army not joining any Albania mission - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: German army not joining any Albania mission - Kinkel.

text.p: Germany's Foreign Minister said on Friday Bonn did not plan to deploy its troops in a possible international peace-keeping mission to Albania and was "extremely sceptical" about the success of such a plan.

Kinkel told Germany's second television programme, ZDF, he agreed with both Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, who said earlier they doubted an international mission could help the impoverished Balkan state.

He was speaking after special European envoy to Albania Austrian Franz Vranitsky said he saw no alternative to Western military intervention to halt the anarchy and chaos spreading through Albania and urged immediate action.
Asked if German troops should take part in such a mission, Kinkel said: "I am extremely sceptical and no, I don't think so, although one should never said never."
Kinkel echoed the words of Kohl who said earlier the Albanian crisis was an internal matter and that it was unclear what any western military force would do if sent there.

"Neither NATO, nor the United Nations nor the Europeans are keen on the idea (of a mission)," Kinkel said, adding that European Union foreign ministers would discuss the situation in Albania on Saturday.

Kinkel said it was important to ensure the trouble did not spill over across the border to Macedonia or any other neighbours, such as the Serb province of Kosovo, populated mainly by ethnic Albanians.

Vranitzky, who is a special envoy for the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe (OSCE), made the proposal after meeting Albanian government leaders and representatives of rebel southern towns on an Italian frigate Aliseo in the Adriatic.
